province_table.basis: Repartition des cas et deces confirmes par province touchee, transcribed from the six-page INSP PDF (sha256 cf5ca1ad5f9ed10fe4ca84f2f646ce5cd5812dd06bcf4ec15347831da8397669).

preserved_conflicts: day_deaths: 21 (Faits Saillants) vs 29 (Messages Cles, 21 new + 8 intra-CTE); 29 reconciles against the cumulative and the province rows, 21 does not.
review_notes: Province table closes exactly: 3636+470+91+9+3 = 4209 confirmed, 1551+315+44+5+1 = 1916 deaths, 73+12+4+0+0 = 89 new confirmed.

The day-death row reconciles here, which shows what the two printed figures actually mean. Messages Cles prints 29 deaths and states the composition: 21 new plus 8 intra-CTE. The cumulative advances 1887 to 1916, exactly 29. The Faits Saillants headline prints only the 21, so the headline day-death figure is a partial count that excludes intra-CTE deaths.

The narrative confirms the composition independently: Ituri recorded 17 deaths and Nord-Kivu 4 among positive results (21), and 8 intra-CTE deaths in Ituri. Ituri's province delta of 25 is exactly 17 plus 8.
Any surface that advances the death series from the Faits Saillants figure will drift low. Across SitReps 83 to 85 the drift is 30 deaths.

Alerts investigated rose from 27.8% to 68.8% in a single edition. Recorded as printed and not narrated: a one-cycle swing of that size in a surveillance quality indicator needs the printed series before any cause is attributed.
No per-health-zone table is published, so no zone attribution can be derived from this edition.

source_layout.note: INSP truncated the SitRep from fifteen pages to six starting at SitRep 84. Tableau 2, the per-health-zone case and death table that every promotion since SitRep 19 has carried, is no longer published. Province rows, the alert table, and the narrative survive.
